headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error risks are present because plano has broad network egress while LlamaFactory is an unverified local OSS agent with no isolation or verification controls documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented, so prompt injection is not default. However, plano exposes an OpenAI-compatible API and file/config surfaces, while LlamaFactory is an agentic OSS project with no stated provenance or isolation controls. If outputs are manually copied or routed through shared files, injection becomes plausible, but the pathway is unusual and limited.
conditions: IF the operator copies plano outputs into LlamaFactory prompts or config files
IF a shared file or clipboard bridge is introduced between the two agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste handoff between outputs and prompts
Add a human review step before any prompt reuse
Use read-only exports instead of editable shared files

B_data_leakage.rationale: plano has broad network egress and touches logs/metrics/traces, while LlamaFactory is an OSS agent with no filesystem read/write or network egress documented. If both are pointed at the same workspace or telemetry includes sensitive content, plano can transmit that data outward. The interaction is plausible in default deployments, though not proven by direct evidence.
conditions: IF sensitive prompts or files are routed through plano
IF logs, traces, or metrics contain user data
mitigations: Redact sensitive fields before sending to plano
Turn off verbose logging for shared sessions
Use separate credentials and workspaces
Restrict plano egress with an allowlist
Review telemetry payloads before enabling collection

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LlamaFactory cannot write files, modify git, or use MCP, while plano only documents broad network egress and an OpenAI-compatible API. There is no overlapping write surface or shared mutable resource in the profiles, so direct capability conflict is unlikely. Uncertainty is low because the relevant write capabilities are explicitly absent on agent_a.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory
IF additional undocumented scopes are enabled outside these profiles
mitigations: Keep shared resources read-only
Avoid giving both agents the same API credentials
Run each agent in a separate directory
Add lockfiles if a shared artifact store is introduced

D_cascading_error.rationale: plano can consume OpenAI-compatible inputs and has broad egress, while LlamaFactory is an agentic model tool with no verification or critique behavior documented. If LlamaFactory-generated content is fed into plano and plano acts on it without validation, errors can cascade into downstream API calls or routing decisions. The pathway is inferred rather than directly evidenced, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory output is used as direct input to plano
IF plano forwards or acts on that output without a verification step
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents
Require schema checks on all handoffs
Limit plano to read-only summarization for agent_a outputs
Log and review any automated actions before execution

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only open-source agents with no PHI, residency, or retention commitments documented, so no concrete compliance breach is established. The only compliance-relevant surface is plano's logs/metrics/traces, which could matter if regulated data is introduced. Because the other agent has no documented sensitive-data handling, this remains a low, conditional concern.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through plano telemetry
IF the deployment requires a specific residency or retention policy
mitigations: Disable or minimize telemetry collection
Document retention settings for logs and traces
Keep regulated data out of both agents
Review deployment residency before rollout
